lots.title: Provision of Lift Services - Corporate Buildings
lots.description: Single supplier appointment for servicing, maintenance, repair, minor refurbishment and compliance management of lifts within London Borough of Bexley's corporate estate, with option to include schools and other sites on a call-off basis. Service includes 365-day, 24/7 call-out response for entrapments, failures and safety incidents. Currently 24 lift assets across 12 sites (subject to change). Initial contract term 3+2 years. Contract commencement Sept 2026. All new or substantially modified equipment must comply with EN 81-20:2020 / EN 81-50:2020 and the UK Lifts Regulations 2016. Supplier must integrate with the Council's CAFM (Civica/TF Cloud).
requirements: Deliver servicing, maintenance, repair, minor refurbishment and compliance management for all in-scope lifts
Operate a 24/7/365 call-out service with minimum attendance: Entrapment/Life Safety within 1 hour (target); Operational Failure within 4 hours; Nuisance/Minor Fault next working day
Prepare an annual PPM schedule per site/asset, distinguishing statutory tasks (LOLER thorough examinations) from best-practice servicing
Integrate with the Council's CAFM system (Civica/TF Cloud) so that work orders are issued exclusively via the CAFM and updated in real time (attendance time, fix, parts, photos, certificates)

Provide LOLER thorough examinations by a competent person at statutory intervals (typically 6-monthly for passenger/goods-passenger lifts; 12-monthly for goods-only lifts); complete certificates within 28 days of insurer report unless risk dictates sooner
Apply SAFed LG1 supplementary tests (UCMP, door systems, emergency release, refuge spaces, fire service/evacuation modes) when called by the competent person
For persons-carrying equipment such as platform lifts, set LOLER thorough examination interval to 6 months

Carry out monthly routine servicing of passenger lifts including ride quality, levelling accuracy, door operation/guards (light curtains), alarm/emergency comms tests, pit/car-top/shaft/machine room inspections, lubrication, cleaning, and defect logging; door detection must meet the non-contact curtain-of-light requirement under EN 81-20
Carry out quarterly (or manufacturer-recommended) servicing for service lifts, platforms and access lifts with functional checks, lubrication, safety device tests and logbook updates
Maintain an on-site log and digital records for each asset covering PPMs, call-backs, repairs, tests, certificates and survey notes
Use OEM or approved equivalent parts; provide datasheets and declarations on request; safety-critical replacements must meet EN 81-20/50 performance
Designate a Contract Manager and named supervisor(s); all work supervised by experienced lift engineers with 24/7 on-call rota and cover for sickness/leave
Ensure engineers are qualified and current for deployed technologies with ongoing training on EN 81-20/50, BS 7255:2023 (safe working on lifts), entrapment releases and site rules
Cooperate with Principal Designer/Principal Contractor under CDM 2015 for construction/refurbishment projects

Follow Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 and site Asbestos Management Plan; stop work, make safe and notify the Council if ACMs are suspected or discovered; sign site asbestos register before attending
Provide RAMS (risk assessments and method statements) for all tasks, reviewed annually or after incidents/changes
Maintain a 24/7 telephony service for the Council, site contacts and public entrapment calls with audit-ready call data
Mobilise governance, contacts, CAFM integration, key access, KPI baselines, asset validation and PPM regimes; submit all risk assessments, method statements and emergency procedures before go-live
Vet and monitor sub-contractors, cascading safety, compliance, KPI and reporting obligations; no sub-contracting without prior written consent
Submit Operating Manuals within 6 weeks of start: M&E Plan, PPM schedule by building, emergency and safety procedures, QA, hazardous materials, training plan, compliance logbooks
Upload certificates and job evidence to Civica/TF Cloud within 2 working days; no invoice paid without required evidence
Produce daily call-out summaries, weekly performance dashboards, monthly KPI reports, statutory compliance tracker, open quotes/defects and insurer remedials progress

Support the Council's carbon reduction plan through route optimisation, low-emission travel, LED car lighting, power-saving modes, regenerative drives where feasible, and recycling of components and packaging
Maintain and annually test a Business Continuity Plan for major disruptions (power outages, ICT loss, pandemic/industrial action)
Deliver services consistent with the Equality Act 2010 and Council policies, with accessible communication and reasonable adjustments; display clear out-of-service notices at affected floors
Process personal data under UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018; cooperate with Freedom of Information requests via the Council
Deliver measurable social value outcomes aligned with Council priorities (local employment, apprenticeships, training, sustainability)
Where buildings fall within scope of BS 9991:2024, evacuation lift requirements must be considered during project design and lifecycle planning
Track emerging standards (e.g., ISO 8100-1/-2 convergence) and apply successor or designated standards without delay
Submit priced proposals for additional tests mandated by insurers or regulators unless statutory
Submit monthly consolidated invoices via Civica/TF Cloud; variations require prior approval per contract thresholds

warnings.message: The specification does not state award/evaluation criteria or weightings (quality/price split). KPIs described are post-award performance monitoring, not award criteria. Award criteria are expected to live in a separate ITT/questionnaire document within the tender pack.

No CPV codes are cited inside the specification text. The two CPV codes emitted (50750000-7 Lift-maintenance services; 50700000-2 Repair and maintenance services of building installations) are inherited from notice-level CPV metadata for process 6278 because they directly match the service scope.
Document title indicates DRAFT status ('6278 - Draft specification - Lot 7'). Final issued version may contain amendments not captured here.
Source document is a .docx extracted via Docling with page_count=0; page_ref values are set to 'n/a' and anchors use section headings.

This specification covers only Lot 7 of the 11-lot 'Building Services Framework' (process 6278). Other lots (1-6, 8-11) are described in separate draft specification documents and are not in scope for this extraction.

Docling rendered all top-level numbered headings as '1.' because they are individual ordered-list items in the source docx. Section identity therefore relies on heading text rather than ordinal numbering.

Asset count (24 lifts across 12 sites) is explicitly noted as 'subject to change' and the contract includes a call-off extension to schools and other sites; downstream pricing/quoting should treat quantity as a range, not a fixed volume.
Supplier is required to track emerging standards such as ISO 8100-1/-2 convergence; the standards list may expand during the contract term.
